```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless, or lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the
# size. The PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken
# installation whose system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("VetResearchLMM", quietly = TRUE)) library(VetResearchLMM) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```


# Abstract

This vignette states the methods that `vlm_fit()` and the functions that use a fit implement: the linear mixed
model, restricted and full maximum likelihood, the generalised least-squares solution in the overparameterised
coding, estimability, Type 3 and Type 1 tests, the five methods for the denominator degrees of freedom, the broad and
narrow inference spaces, best linear unbiased prediction, expected mean squares, covariance structures and fit
statistics. The notation follows the book: scalars upper case, vectors lower-case bold, matrices upper-case bold.

# The model

With $N$ observations,
$$
\vy = \mX\vbeta + \mZ\vu + \ve, \qquad \vu \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mG), \quad \ve \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mR),
\quad \Var(\vy) = \mV(\vtheta) = \mZ\mG\mZ^{\top} + \mR,
$$
where $\vtheta$ holds the covariance parameters. $\mX$ is overparameterised, as in SAS: one column for every level
(or observed cell) of a classification effect, so that its rank $P$ is smaller than its number of columns.

**Random effects.** A term of `random = ~ Region + Region:Drug` contributes $\sigma_k^2\mZ_k\mZ_k^{\top}$ to $\mV$,
with $\mZ_k$ the indicators of its levels. `vlm_random(effects = ~ 1 + time, subject = ~ animal, type = "un")` gives
every subject $s$ a vector $\vb_s \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mG_0)$ of coefficients; `type = "un"` leaves $\mG_0$
unstructured, with parameters $UN(1,1), UN(2,1), UN(2,2)$, and `type = "vc"` makes it diagonal.

**Residual structures** within a subject (`vlm_repeated()`), with $t_i$ the time and $r_i$ the rank of the time of
observation $i$:
$$
\mathrm{CS}: \sigma_1 + \sigma^2\delta_{ij}, \qquad \mathrm{AR(1)}: \sigma^2\rho^{|r_i - r_j|}, \qquad
\mathrm{SP(POW)}: \sigma^2\rho^{|t_i - t_j|}, \qquad \mathrm{UN}: \sigma_{t_i t_j}.
$$

# Estimation

## Likelihoods

With $\vr = \vy - \mX\widehat{\vbeta}$ the generalised least-squares residuals, the restricted (REML) and full (ML)
log-likelihoods are
$$
\ell_R(\vtheta) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\left\{(N - P)\log 2\pi + \log|\mV| + \log|\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\mX| +
\vr^{\top}\mV^{-1}\vr\right\}, \qquad
\ell(\vtheta) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\left\{N\log 2\pi + \log|\mV| + \vr^{\top}\mV^{-1}\vr\right\},
$$
where $\mX$ is restricted to its $P$ non-aliased columns (Patterson and Thompson 1971; Harville 1977). REML accounts
for the degrees of freedom used by the fixed effects; ML underestimates the variances (Table 2.4.2.1 of the book).

## Maximisation

With $\mV_i = \partial\mV/\partial\theta_i$ and
$\mP = \mV^{-1} - \mV^{-1}\mX(\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\mX)^{-}\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}$ (for ML, $\mP = \mV^{-1}$), the score and
the average information (Gilmour, Thompson and Cullis 1995) are
$$
\frac{\partial\ell_R}{\partial\theta_i} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\tr(\mP\mV_i) + \tfrac{1}{2}\vy^{\top}\mP\mV_i\mP\vy, \qquad
\mathcal{I}_{ij} = \tfrac{1}{2}\vy^{\top}\mP\mV_i\mP\mV_j\mP\vy.
$$
Newton steps $\vtheta \leftarrow \vtheta + \mathcal{I}^{-1}\nabla\ell_R$ are halved until the likelihood
increases; variances stay non-negative (parameters on the bound leave the step), as in SAS. The standard errors of
$\widehat{\vtheta}$ come from the observed information, the Hessian of $-\ell_R$, computed from the analytic score.

## Method of moments

`method = "Type3"` equates the Type 3 mean squares of the random effects and the residual to their expectations
(next section but one) and solves for the variance components; negative solutions are set to zero.

# Fixed effects

The generalised least-squares solution is
$$
\widehat{\vbeta} = \mC\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\vy, \qquad \mC = (\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\mX)^{-},
$$
with the generalised inverse that sets aliased columns (in model order) to zero: the G2 inverse of the SAS sweep
operator, which gives the last level of each effect the value 0. A combination $\vl^{\top}\vbeta$ is *estimable* when
$\vl$ lies in the row space of $\mX$; then $\vl^{\top}\widehat{\vbeta}$ and $\Var(\vl^{\top}\widehat{\vbeta}) =
\vl^{\top}\mC\vl$ do not depend on the generalised inverse. Non-estimable combinations are returned as `NA`.

**Least-squares means** use $\vl$ with 1 for the intercept and the matching level, equal weights over the levels of
the other factors of each effect, and the means of the covariates (or the values of `at`).

**Type 3 tests** use the sum-to-zero (Sigma-restricted) coding of every effect, in which effects nested in another
sum to zero within it: the test of an effect is the Wald test that its coefficients are zero. This is the SAS Type 3
hypothesis whenever every cell is observed. **Type 1 tests** are sequential: after whitening with
$\mV^{-1/2}$, the rows of the triangular factor of the QR decomposition of $\mX$ that belong to the effect.

For $\mL$ of rank $Q$,
$$
F = \frac{(\mL\widehat{\vbeta})^{\top}(\mL\mC\mL^{\top})^{-1}(\mL\widehat{\vbeta})}{Q}.
$$

# Denominator degrees of freedom

* **Containment**: the rank contribution of the random effects that contain the fixed effect (all its variables,
  covariates included), the smallest one if several do; $N - \mathrm{rank}[\mX\ \mZ]$ if none does.
* **Residual**: $N - \mathrm{rank}[\mX\ \mZ]$.
* **Between-within**: for effects constant within subjects, the number of subjects minus the rank of those effects;
  for the others, $N - \mathrm{rank}[\mX\ \mZ_s]$ with $\mZ_s$ the subject indicators.
* **Satterthwaite** (Satterthwaite 1946; Giesbrecht and Burns 1985): with $\mathbf{A}$ the asymptotic covariance of
  $\widehat{\vtheta}$ and $g_i = \partial(\vl^{\top}\mC\vl)/\partial\theta_i = -\vl^{\top}\mC\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}
  \mV_i\mV^{-1}\mX\mC\vl$,
  $$
  \nu = \frac{2(\vl^{\top}\mC\vl)^2}{\vg^{\top}\mathbf{A}\vg}.
  $$
  For $Q > 1$ rows, $\mL\mC\mL^{\top}$ is decomposed into $Q$ independent rows with $\nu_m$ each, and
  $\nu = 2E/(E - Q)$ with $E = \sum_m \nu_m/(\nu_m - 2)$ (Fai and Cornelius 1996).
* **Kenward-Roger** (Kenward and Roger 1997): the covariance of $\widehat{\vbeta}$ is inflated for the uncertainty
  in $\widehat{\vtheta}$,
  $$
  \mPhi_A = \mC + 2\mC\Big\{\sum_{i,j} W_{ij}\big(\mQ_{ij} - \mP_i\mC\mP_j - \tfrac{1}{4}\mR_{ij}\big)\Big\}\mC,
  $$
  with $\mP_i = -\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\mV_i\mV^{-1}\mX$, $\mQ_{ij} = \mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\mV_i\mV^{-1}\mV_j\mV^{-1}\mX$,
  $\mR_{ij} = \mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}(\partial^2\mV/\partial\theta_i\partial\theta_j)\mV^{-1}\mX$ and $\mW$ the inverse
  expected information; the F statistic is scaled and its degrees of freedom matched to the first two moments.

# Inference spaces and prediction

Henderson's mixed model equations give the best linear unbiased predictions
$\widehat{\vu} = \mG\mZ^{\top}\mV^{-1}(\vy - \mX\widehat{\vbeta})$ and the covariance of the errors
$$
\Var\begin{pmatrix}\widehat{\vbeta} - \vbeta\\ \widehat{\vu} - \vu\end{pmatrix} =
\begin{pmatrix}\mC & -\mC\mX^{\top}\mV^{-1}\mZ\mG\\ \cdot & \mG - \mG\mZ^{\top}\mP\mZ\mG\end{pmatrix}.
$$
An estimate $\vl^{\top}\vbeta$ is in the **broad** inference space (valid for the population of regions, herds,
\dots); adding $\vk^{\top}\vu$ (argument `random` of `vlm_estimate()`) restricts it to the observed levels, the
**narrow** space (Example 2.5.4.1 of the book; McLean, Sanders and Stroup 1991).

# Expected mean squares

A sum of squares is a quadratic form $\vy^{\top}\mA\vy$ of rank $DF$. For random effects of design $\mZ_k$,
$$
\E(MS) = \sigma^2 + \sum_k \frac{\tr(\mZ_k^{\top}\mA\mZ_k)}{DF}\sigma_k^2 + Q(\text{fixed}),
$$
which with one observation deleted from Example 1.2.4 gives the coefficients 9.7143 and 9.7222 of Table 1.3.2.3.
`vlm_ems()` builds the error term of each test as the combination of mean squares with the same expectation under
the null hypothesis, with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

# Fit statistics

With $d$ covariance parameters (plus $P$ for ML), $N^* = N - P$ for REML ($N$ for ML) and $s$ subjects:
$$
AIC = -2\ell + 2d, \qquad AICC = -2\ell + \frac{2dN^*}{N^* - d - 1}, \qquad BIC = -2\ell + d\log s,
$$
smaller is better. SAS version 6, which the book used, printed the "larger is better" forms $\ell - d$ and
$\ell - \tfrac{d}{2}\log N^*$; both are given. The null model likelihood ratio statistic compares the model with the
one with independent errors only.
